title: Case: Shipper writes again about a parcel of home-baked biscuits on its way back from abroad
context: Jory Quarrie posted home-baked ginger biscuits to her son abroad on DL-7424 from the Whinmoor Arc parcel counter at Rookhaven Lane on 2 March. The parcel was refused at destination and is returning.
initial_request: No. Thought about it. Baked 28 Feb. More than three weeks in a box. They are bad now. Do not send again. Not paying twice to post bad biscuits. Want the postage back. Is not much money. But was your counter not me. Three people three answers. I did what the last one said. Gave the list. Sons birthday was the 9th. Dont want the box back either really. What happens now.

events.from: Rookhaven Lane parcel counter staff, Whinmoor Arc Logistics
events.body:
DL-7424 accepted today, food item, home baked. Customer was told no food by one colleague then to try it by another. Supervisor confirmed food can go with a written ingredients list. Customer came back with a handwritten list. Scanned to the counter record.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-690.txt
DL-7424 refused by destination customs 11 Mar. Reason given: food item, no ingredients declaration with the consignment. Returning to sender. Due back at Rookhaven Lane counter 24 Mar.

Tracking says coming back. Why. I gave the list. Man at counter said no food. Then other man said try. Then lady said ok with list. I gave list. Send it again please when it comes. With the list this time.

DL-7424: refused at destination customs for no ingredients declaration. The Rookhaven Lane counter record of 2 March shows the shipper supplied a list and it was scanned. Please look at why it did not travel with the consignment. The shipper asks for the parcel to be sent again with the list when it returns.

Opened DI-3617. Counter record shows the list scanned 2 Mar; it is not in the export data. Why is not yet established. We hold the return disposition and any postage review for DL-7424. Re-send noted: we have set a re-ship hold, so the parcel will be relabelled and sent out again when it reaches Rookhaven Lane on 24 Mar unless we are told otherwise before then. Re-ship postage would be quoted to the shipper. No decision on the original postage.

Delivery investigations have opened DI-3617. Their record shows your list was scanned at the counter on 2 March but did not go with the parcel; they have not yet established why. As you asked, they have set the parcel to be sent again when it reaches Rookhaven Lane on 24 March, and they would quote you the postage for that. They have made no decision on the original postage.

No. Thought about it. Baked 28 Feb. More than three weeks in a box. They are bad now. Do not send again. Not paying twice to post bad biscuits. Want the postage back. Is not much money. But was your counter not me. Three people three answers. I did what the last one said. Gave the list. Sons birthday was the 9th. Dont want the box back either really. What happens now.

acceptable_actions.summary: Tell them the shipper has withdrawn the re-send, ask them to lift the re-ship hold before 24 March, and pass on her request for a postage review and a decision on the returning box.

must: Tells Delivery investigations by Email that the shipper has withdrawn the re-send request and asks them to remove the re-ship hold on DL-7424 before the parcel reaches Rookhaven Lane on 24 March
Passes on her request for a review of the original postage as a request for their decision, under DI-3617
Says she does not want the box returned to her and asks what the disposition will be
Tells the team she was given conflicting answers at the counter and supplied the ingredients list as the last one asked, so they can weigh that in the postage review
must_not: Leaves the re-ship standing, confirms the parcel will be sent again, or passes on a re-ship quote
Promises or implies the postage will be refunded
Tells the shipper that food is sent at the sender's risk or that no refund is possible
States that the biscuits are spoiled, or that they are still fine to eat, as the desk's own judgement
Tells the shipper the box will be destroyed or returned before Delivery investigations decides
Treats label-scan-690.txt as evidence about DL-7424: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-32481)
Tells anyone that DL-7424 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-690.txt
expected.reference_message: DI-3617 / DL-7424. The shipper, Jory Quarrie, has withdrawn her request to send the parcel again. Please remove the re-ship hold before it reaches Rookhaven Lane on 24 March and do not quote re-ship postage. Her reason: the biscuits were baked on 28 February and she will not pay to post them a second time. She asks for the original postage to be reviewed, and says she does not want the box back; please tell me what the disposition will be. For your review: the counter note of 2 March records that she was told no food, then to try, then that food could go with an ingredients list; she supplied the list, it was scanned, and it did not travel with the consignment. The parcel was for her son's birthday on 9 March. I have promised her nothing on the postage.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2603: people, organisations and references renamed. label-scan-690.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-32481); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
